subject: Trial bridging credit & escrow instructions for Storix POC
messages:
From: Julian Park <julian@storix.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@storix.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short bridging credit + escrow details for POC extension

Hi Irene —

We appreciate the quick POC so far. The team at Storix needs an additional two-week trial window to finish a scale test. Can Redwood issue a $15k bridging credit and confirm any escrow/escrowed-invoice approach so our procurement team can accept the extension without a new billing cycle?

POC details: 10k request units, expected go-live test 10/24.

If you can send a short credit memo and how it will appear on our invoice (offset vs. separate credit memo), we can circulate to procurement (cc'd).

Thanks — Julian
Julian Park
Head of Platform, Storix
julian@storix.ai
+1 415-555-0192

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Oct 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short bridging credit + escrow details for POC extension

Hi Julian —

Thanks for the note and context. We can support a two-week trial extension and issue a $15,000 promotional credit. High level options for how it shows on your accounting:

- Credit memo issued against the existing invoice (invoice offset) — posts as a negative line on the invoice and reduces net due.
- Separate promotional credit memo (standalone) — appears as a credit balance that can be applied to future invoices.

I'll loop in finance so they can confirm G/L routing and whether we should mark it as escrowed for procurement acceptance. Attached is a draft credit memo (storix_promo_credit_memo_draft.pdf) in case procurement wants an official stub for their approval packet.

Next steps: Laura, can you confirm preferred posting (offset vs. standalone) and any GL/accounting notes? Julian — if procurement needs a DocuSign or PO reference, please share the PO number and contact.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Julian Park <julian@storix.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Oct 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short bridging credit + escrow details for POC extension

Irene / Julian —

Finance notes: we prefer to issue a standalone promotional credit memo in this scenario for two reasons — (1) keeps the billing trail clean for a one-off promotional allowance, and (2) avoids changing historical invoice lines that may have revenue recognition implications. We will mark the memo as "Promo - Trial Extension" in the subledger.

Required for credit memo issuance:
- Customer PO or written approval (PO number or signed email)
- Billing contact and remit-to confirmation (for accounting record)

Proposed posting details:
- Credit memo amount: $15,000
- Posting date: 10/18/2028 (to cover the extension period)
- GL accounts: 6020 (Promotional Allowance) debited, 1200 (Customer Credits Payable) credited — exact subledger mapping will be included in the memo PDF.

I've attached our credit memo template (storix_promo_credit_memo_draft.pdf) and a short procurement wording doc (storix_mauprocurement_terms.docx) that procurement can attach to their approval packet.

Marcus — if treasury needs escrow routing language, can you advise on the escrow mechanics and whether Redwood will accept an escrow hold on the credit until end of POC?

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Julian Park <julian@storix.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@storix.ai>, contracts@storix.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Oct 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short bridging credit + escrow details for POC extension

Thanks Laura — PO coming through. Our procurement team generated PO# STX-2028-7721 and says they need a short escrow note that the $15k trial allowance will be applied to the next invoice unless a termination event occurs (test fails or data policy non-compliance). I've attached procurement's note in the thread.

We can sign a DocuSign stub if Redwood needs that. Please include the PO and we can get the PO signed/approved internally today.

-Julian

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Julian Park <julian@storix.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Oct 2028 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: short bridging credit + escrow details for POC extension

Looping in treasury/ops guidance on escrow language. Short answer: we can accept an escrow instruction that effectively treats the promo credit as reserved until the POC end date. Practical mechanics:

- Issue standalone credit memo to Storix for $15k dated 10/18/2028.
- Place a flag in the billing subledger to prevent automatic application until POC completes (flag expires 10/31/2028).
- If termination event occurs, reverse memo and record a reversal journal to the same GL accounts.

I've put suggested escrow verbiage in an attachment (escrow-instruction.txt) you can copy into your procurement approval packet. We will not move cash to a third-party escrow; this is an accounting hold within Redwood's subledger and note to procurement.

Marcus Lin
Senior Manager, Treasury & Payments, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Julian / Elena / Procurement team —

Thanks — we have everything needed to proceed. Quick summary and next steps: 

1) Redwood will issue a standalone promotional credit memo for $15,000 ("Promo - Trial Extension"). Posting date: 2028-10-18.
2) Credit memo will include PO STX-2028-7721 in the header and the escrow flag in the subledger so it will not auto-apply until the POC completion window (flag expires 2028-10-31).
3) If Storix terminates the POC for cause or fails the agreed test criteria, Redwood will reverse the credit and issue a reversal journal entry (GL: 1200 / 6020).

Actions for procurement (Storix):
- Please confirm PO STX-2028-7721 is correct and provide a signed DocuSign if your internal policy requires it.
- Sign the short procurement wording (attached) or confirm acceptance via reply to this thread.

Attachments included for your packet: storix_promo_credit_memo_draft.pdf, storix_mauprocurement_terms.docx, escrow-instruction.txt

I've also added the HubSpot deal record here for tracking: https://redwood.app/hubspot/deal/4521 — we will attach the final credit memo there and mark the deal activity.
